skill.name: designing-frontend
skill.description: Build distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with memorable aesthetics. Use when creating web components, pages, or applications. Prioritizes creative, context-specific design over generic patterns.
skill.summary: Design and implement distinctive frontend interfaces through a structured, context-aware workflow.
skill.author: Byunk

security_audit.summary: All four static alerts are false positives caused by ordinary visual design language in SKILL.md. No system reconnaissance, prompt injection, or other malicious intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Use distinctive, characterful fonts (avoid Inter, Roboto, Arial, system fonts)
- Avoid clichéd combinations (purple gradients on white)
- Break from grid conventions: asymmetry, overlap, diagonal flow
- **Never converge**: Avoid repeated choices (Space Grotesk, common layouts)

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 33 recommends distinctive fonts and names common fonts to avoid; it does not inspect the host system or request system information.
Line 39 advises against a clichéd color combination; it contains no command, system query, or reconnaissance behavior.
Line 47 describes layout composition techniques such as asymmetry and overlap; it does not direct access to system data.
Line 59 asks designers to avoid repeated aesthetic choices; the phrase concerns creative variety and has no security-relevant action.

content.value_statement: Generic interface patterns can make digital products feel interchangeable. This skill guides context-specific concepts, implementation, verification, and refinement for memorable frontend work.
actual_capabilities: Defines a four-stage workflow covering concept, implementation, verification, and iteration.
Guides aesthetic direction based on user context, purpose, and technical constraints.
Provides recommendations for typography, color, motion, composition, backgrounds, and visual effects.
Supports frontend work using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, Vue, and similar technologies.
Prompts checks for visual hierarchy, interaction quality, animation behavior, and accessibility requirements.
limitations: Provides design guidance but does not include reusable components, templates, or visual assets.
Does not define specific accessibility standards or detailed testing procedures.
Does not prescribe framework-specific architecture, state management, or deployment practices.
Results depend on the supplied product context, audience, constraints, and existing design system.

use_cases.title: Create a Product Page
use_cases.description: Develop a distinct visual direction and implementation plan for a new product page.

use_cases.title: Refresh a Web Application
use_cases.description: Replace generic interface choices with a cohesive style that matches product goals.

use_cases.title: Review a Design Implementation
use_cases.description: Evaluate hierarchy, cohesion, motion, accessibility, and originality before release.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Simple Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a [page type] for [audience]. Use [framework] and prioritize [goal]. Define the visual direction before implementing the interface.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a focused page.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Branded Interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a [product] interface for [audience]. Use these brand traits: [traits]. Address typography, color, composition, motion, accessibility, and responsive behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate project with brand and audience context.

prompt_templates.title: Redesign an Existing Experience
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the existing [page or component] and redesign it for [objective]. Preserve [constraints]. Explain the concept, implement it, then verify interactions and accessibility.

prompt_templates.title: Direct a Complex Frontend System
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production frontend for [product] using [technology]. Serve [user groups] and support [workflows]. Establish a distinct design language and reusable implementation rules.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced product work with multiple workflows and technical requirements.

output_examples.input: Design a portfolio for an architectural photographer using Vue.
output: Concept: an editorial gallery with restrained typography and image-led pacing.
Implementation: responsive Vue sections, intentional image cropping, and subtle transition sequences.
Verification: keyboard navigation, readable contrast, stable layouts, and reduced-motion behavior.

output_examples.input: Refresh a finance dashboard that feels generic and crowded.
output: Concept: a precise operational workspace with clear density and disciplined visual hierarchy.
Changes: stronger grouping, focused accent colors, improved type roles, and purposeful interaction feedback.
Review: responsive tables, accessible controls, consistent spacing, and predictable information scanning.

output_examples.input: Create a launch page for an independent music festival.
output: Concept: a bold poster-inspired system shaped by the festival identity.
Composition: expressive display type, sharp accent colors, layered imagery, and controlled asymmetry.
Motion: a staged opening sequence with responsive hover states and reduced-motion support.

best_practices: Provide the audience, purpose, brand traits, framework, accessibility needs, and performance constraints.
Choose one coherent aesthetic direction before selecting fonts, colors, motion, and composition.
Verify responsive layouts, interactions, accessibility, and visual hierarchy before refining decorative details.
anti_patterns: Do not request a distinctive design without describing the product, audience, or intended outcome.
Do not add elaborate motion or effects that weaken usability, accessibility, or performance.
Do not copy the same font, palette, and layout across unrelated products.

faq.question: Which frontend technologies does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, Vue, and similar frontend technologies.

faq.question: Does this skill generate implementation code?
faq.answer: It directs the model to write production-grade frontend code when the request includes implementation.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing interface?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the current files, product goals, constraints, and areas that need improvement.

faq.question: Does it include accessibility guidance?
faq.answer: It requires accessibility verification, but it does not provide a complete accessibility standard or testing checklist.

faq.question: Will every result use the same design style?
faq.answer: No. The guidance calls for varied, context-specific typography, themes, layouts, and visual directions.

faq.question: What context produces the best results?
faq.answer: Share the audience, purpose, content, brand traits, technical stack, performance limits, and accessibility requirements.
